statement: How many prime numbers are greater than $30$ and less than $50$?

choices.misconception: I counted $49$ as a prime because it is odd and not divisible by $3$ or $5$, but $49 = 7 \cdot 7$.
I listed the odd numbers from $31$ to $49$ and crossed out only the multiples of $3$, leaving $31, 35, 37, 41, 43, 47, 49$.
I listed the odd numbers from $31$ to $49$ and crossed out only the multiples of $5$, leaving $8$ numbers.
I thought every odd number is prime, so I counted all $10$ odd numbers from $31$ to $49$.

hints: Only odd numbers can be primes here. List them.
A number below $50$ is prime if no prime up to $7$ divides it (since $7^2 = 49$ and $8^2 = 64$). Check $3$, $5$ and $7$.
Of the odd numbers $31, 33, \ldots, 49$, cross out $33, 39, 45$ (multiples of $3$), $35$ (multiple of $5$) and $49$ (multiple of $7$).

solutions.reliable: The odd numbers between $30$ and $50$ are $31, 33, 35, 37, 39, 41, 43, 45, 47, 49$. Since $\sqrt{49} = 7$, a number here is prime unless $3$, $5$ or $7$ divides it. Crossing out $33, 39, 45$ (multiples of $3$), $35$ (multiple of $5$) and $49$ (multiple of $7$) leaves $31, 37, 41, 43, 47$. That is $5$ primes.
